newsitem.title: UK: Europe stocks hold gains ahead of Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Europe stocks hold gains ahead of Wall Street.

text.p: European stocks held steady in early afternoon trade on Monday following a strong starting rebound from Friday's lows as markets awaited further direction from Wall Street's opening.
Traders said a good showing from Wall Street, backed by soothing comments from key central bankers, should ensure a further rise in key markets before the close.
The recovery had run out of steam at mid-morning amid concern that gains lacked follow-through support.
Markets were rocked on Friday after U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments on Thursday about "irrational exuberance" in world financial markets.
But Bank of England governor Eddie George and Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer both said on Monday that market reaction to the comments was overdone.
"We feel to some extent there was an over-reaction to a question and the markets seem to be stable again," Tietmeyer said after a meeting of G10 central bank governors.
Analysts said they expected Wall Street stocks to open higher, although recent bullishness may be tempered.
"I don't think the market's going to be as exuberent," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities.
Greenspan's remarks raised concern about a possible tightening in U.S. monetary policy, which boosted the dollar on Monday morning.
In London, the FTSE 100 index gained over 40 points at one stage but was capped by talk of an early election following the latest outbreak of tensions in the ruling Conservative Party.
The FTSE 100 was 31.1 points higher at 3,994.1 at 1435 GMT after ending Friday 88.2 points off at 3,963.0 -- its biggest one-day loss in percentage terms since February 1994.
German shares rushed ahead after Friday's dive as a firmer dollar and Bunds lent support. Analysts and traders said the market's upward trend was intact, and viewed Friday's fall as an overreaction.
"I am totally bullish. The market had the weekend to digest what happened last week and is in far calmer form," said on Munich dealer.
The DAX index ended bourse trade up 65.28 points at 2,857.24, a 2.3 percent rise from Friday's close. It earlier touched 2,872.57.
French shares picked up again in afternoon trade after drifting off highs earlier.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 16.87 points at 2,257.59 at 1417 GMT.
Dutch shares were firmer, but were holding back ahead of Wall Street's open. The AEX index was 6.46 points up at 622.72, against an early high of 624.28.
Austrian shares rebounded 1.26 percent and traders said the market looked to have overcome last Friday's sharp fall and resumed its upward march.
Leading Russian shares edged up in a correction with low volumes and wide spreads, reflecting traders' uncertainty over where the market was headed.
Danish shares rose 0.27 percent in a restrained recovery.
